I think Extella is the worst entry in the Extraverse series due to how it just ♥♥♥♥♥ on any base material.
The story starts semi-ok, the ending from Extra got retconned, but that's fine and can be forgiven. You start with following Nero, which isn't too bad.
But then comes the kicker, suddenly Tamamo is also there, and she recognizes you as her Master, she mentions that she was your sub-party Servant (Suddenly you had 2 Servants in Fate/Extra?) And just seems to be even more clingy than before, but that can be somewhat forgiven due to her personality being like that.
This is still... somewhat forgiveable.... You complete Nero's story and that's fine, it wasn't as bad as I thought and I quite liked the bittersweet ending (Nero gets a bad ending)
You then start Tamamo's story, which is just pure fanservice, its irrelevant to the plot at all and it's just her being cute and kawaii to you because you're her husband, this would be nice if it had anything to do with the plot, but you could literally cut this story out and Extella would be exactly the same..
It has a good ending which is nice, but that's about it.
Then starts Altera's route (The newly introduced Saber and main villain)
God this route is SO BAD, there are 2 Alteras (Titan Altera and Servant Altera) While one is a murder kill death machine that just plows down everything in its path, the other is a cute, kawaii, shy giant (Titan Altera) she calls you her prisoner, but treats you more like a guest, you're supposed to feel bad for her and then help her..
This is a terrible set up since well.. You're *actively* being the bad guy, and your character knows it, they even mention it.. You kill both your Main and Sub Servant (Nero and Tamamo) and your MC is like "this is fine" which makes absolutely 0 sense.
Then... Starts the true route.... This might be the worst thing in the existance of Fate besides Labyrinth.
You transport your memories from the third route (Altera route) to the you that's with Nero (Nero's route) so now you are the MC with knowledge over both Nero and Altera (but not Tamamo) You get Nero and Tamamo to team up in the end, which is.. okay I guess, since they both love you and want to help you..
But then Archimedes (#2 bad guy) does some spooky♥♥♥♥♥♥to Altera to make her a rampant murder death machine, together with a corrupted version of Liz who just seems to be a jackass and do nothing plot-relevant except meme you.
So you defeat Altera and you're like "noice" but then Archimedes pulls another card out of his♥♥♥♥♥and summons Velber (Some evil comet who annihilates civilizations), that is pretty interesting since it's supposed to be some unstoppable murder death machine 100x the scale of Altera (Tamamo basically gives up for a moment since 'it's all useless anyway' due to Tamamo having experienced this terror before (She is from the Age of Gods and has seen Velber descend once already, where earth almost got wiped) But you kind of convince both Nero and Tamamo to team up anyway.
After Altera dies, she gives her sword of Mars, which she stole from Ares himself, to Nero... Nero then uses the power of Mars and calls it upon herself to transform into 'Saber Venus' which is by definition, the worst character design in all of Fate, you can look it up and you'll see how trash it is, it is pure fanservice.
Then Tamamo is basically told to "sit back in the base and make sure everything is ok" while Saber Venus goes on to save the day with her autistic design and powers, somehow easily beating Velber and Archimedes even though Tamamo, a literal goddess of the Sun, couldn't do something like that... So instead of giving the actual really strong character the oppertunity to assist Nero, she is sidelined and not mentioned again.
So Velber has been defeated and all is well, but then somehow Altera is reborn as Atilla.. This is where it gets bad, Altera is suddenly a loli now ??? And the game ends with a happy end picture of Tamamo, you, Nero and Altera eating dinner, Tamamo seemingly having accepted her role in being part of a Harem, even though in Fate/Extra she mentions several times how much she absolutely hates harems and would castrate her Master if it would ever happen.
Fate Extella completely wipes any character development Tamamo ever got and replaces it with a generic "I love yu master please accept me" stereotype while leaving her on the side, on top of that the game circlejerks Nero literally all the time, and she clearly gets way more than she deserved. The dynamic between Titan Altera and Servant Altera is also just very wrong, and I feel like Altera would've been more interesting as just "Servant Altera" since that one actually had reasons to be like that, while "Titan Altera" was just shy and cute for the sake of making you try to feel bad for wanting to kill her, which really doesn't work.
Now, on to the gameplay... The gameplay feels like a terribly watered down clone of Dynasty Warriors, but without any of the good mechanics, the characters all usually only have 1 optimal combo and it is what you'll be spamming for the majority of the game, the game does not give any incentive to mix stuff up or whatever, you just do the easiest, most AOE hitting and damaging combo your char has, which usually consists out of hitting the same button 4 times and then pressing triangle or right click.
The stages all feel very bland and are being reused several times, there are some nice designs but you get really tired of it when it gets reused like 5 times in a row.
As a final note, since I haven't mentioned it anywhere else.
EMIYA (Nameless Archer) also gets completely shafted to the sideline and doesn't even get any story beyond ' I just joined Nero for mysterious reasons ' and even his side-story doesn't expand on it, all the sidestories with a few exceptions just felt very weak and added close to 0 to the character, they did not feel well made at all and felt more like they were filler because the game isn't actually worth $50.
Fate Extella completely destroys any development Fate/Extra ever gave to all 3 of the protagonist's Servants and instead tries to make it into a bundle of♥♥♥♥♥♥ everything is bad about it, and it has no redeeming factors besides that Archimedes seems like a decently written villain.
Instead of a redemption-like saga for Elizabeth, she instead goes even beyond the boundary of what I thought what was possible to become even more unlikeable, she doesn't do anything relevant in the game except taunt you and your Servant while being a bother to Archimedes.
As a final verdict, I think Fate/Extella is one of the worst Fate material games I've ever seen in my life, and I honestly wish it didn't exist, people always say "Be happy that <your favorite character> gets to star in another game and be good" but that really really isn't the case, I think most Tamamo fans could agree that the game made her worse in every way possible and♥♥♥♥♥♥on the material, Fate/Extra and CCC were much better on their own than the autistic mix that Extella is.
On top of that, the new SHAFT Anime (Fate/Extra Last Encore) Will be the prequel for Fate/Extella instead of following Nero's original route, and from what I've read on Nasu's blog, it is a ♥♥♥♥ing mess.. It truly throws away any development for Tamamo, while Emiya gets a somewhat decent one, but that doesn't matter since he's just forgotten in Extella anyway.
I do not recommend you buy this game because it's really bad in every way possible, the story is bad, the gameplay is bad and the design is bad.. The voice acting is good as always, the char design stays to the original (And adds some nice new outfits for Nero and Tamamo) and the translation is good, there are no complains from me in that regard, the translation was one of the better things.

As of writing this review, I have played roughly 20 hours, so I feel very comfortable giving this game a huge thumbs up.
Coming into the game, I was expecting a cheap Zelda clone that I'd be able to knock out in about 5 hours and then regret the purchase. I've gotta say, I was pleasantly surprised by this game. You can tell that the developers really cared about making a quality product here, and it shows in spades.
So what does this game that so many Zelda clones seem to lack? Heart and charm would be the two biggest aspects, in my opinion.
The heart comes from how the overworld, dungeons and various other locales have all been well fleshed out with secrets and puzzles. You can see that these were not just thrown together all willy nilly, but were constructed with thought and planning for the best gaming experience.
The charm comes from the character interactions (specifically bewteen Khoma and the Red Witch). While the translation does make it hard to understand things at times, it is a rare occurance, and it doesn't detract from the overall experience very much, if at all.
As far as gameplay goes:
-The controls are very tight (I play with a controller, have not tried k+m).
-The puzzles themselves range from easy to challenging. I ran into a couple headscratchers, but nothing that made me ragequit or resort to using a guide.
-Combat is fairly basic, but with enough depth to not make it boring or repetitive. Most people play these games for the exploration aspects anyways, I would imagine.
-The music in this game is really great. Game soundtracks are an important part of enjoying a game for me, and this games soundtrack really delivered.
So to wrap things up, I would highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys Zelda-like adventure games. You will not be disappointed by this one, I assure you. Give it a shot and support a developer that cares about delivering a truly enjoyable gaming experience!

Gun Rocket is a very cool game, but VERY hard. If you wish to try your patience, you can hardly do better than this.
The premise is to move a rocket through space to a target. The challenge being that space, having no gravity, has no means by which to slow or stop your ship, other than its own rockets. So, you fire your ship's rockets to move, to slow, and to change direction. Generally pretty much all at the same time. Thus the challenge is great.
You do all these things in a contrived, shaped space. As such, not only must you do all the above pretty much concurrently, but you must stay within areas of unusual shapes and proportions. Only one level at the time is available for play (so far, at an early level), but 100 levels are available over the life of the game. You are attempting to succeed in reaching the target, but also with the best time and least fuel consumed. Thus, it's possibe to play with great caution, or "hell bent for leather", while consuming fuel rapidly. The feeling of success is substantial!
There is also a multiplayer aspect, which I haven't explored. For this price ($1.99US), you can hardly go wrong.
High recommendation.

Stories of Bethem is quite a charming game. The gameplay compares well to old Zelda games like Link to the Past. You are without a sword, though, and all your abilities use mana instead making mana management important. The abilities/spells you aquire are interesting, they add new fighting mechanics, and unlock new areas for you to explore in both new and already explored maps. Exploration always feels important and rewarding.

Bethem is an action-adventure game built in Game Maker Studio.
Can't say much in regards to the story so far (just started playing), but it seems humorous and doesn't take itself seriously. English translation is a little rough in places (especially in regards to the jokes-lost in translation). There may be a little too much exposition/dialogue given the tone of the story, at least at the start.
If you like Zelda, the action based combat mechanics are very similar to older Zelda games such as Link to the Past or the Gameboy titles.  There is an overworld, there are dungeons and associated puzzles to solve in order to progress. The interface, item mechanics and character abilities are all taken from Zelda.
It includes a very pleasant soundtrack. The sprite work and animations are passable (albeit simplistic). Controller support (xbox) is great, and game feels very responsive; combating monsters and solving puzzles is actually fun and I found myself wanting to complete each area and progress.
There seem to be some problems with running it on modern high-end hardware. I can only play in windowed mode, and have had to disable avast real time scanner every time in order for it to start.
From the perspective of a Zelda fan, this is a pleasant surprise that came out of nowhere. I would recommend it on that basis. But I must caution that it is a little rough/unpolished around the edges for a release title, both technically and in terms of visuals.

If you're a fan of Zelda games for the puzzles, the adventure, the grand scale, seriously consider this game.
Stories of Bethem: Full Moon packs a LOT of content in it's small, unassuming package. Well Elodie is trying to make it to coronation, after her mother’s untimely death, and many dangers stand in front of her. But I assume you know that much already. Long live the queen is a game about making choices, and balancing skills and your mood, to succeed in an array of challenges that lie in your path. From making decisions about your kingdom, to being ambushed on travels and those stupid royal balls.
The first few play throughs I had went a lot like this.
- Oh, look I think I’m doing ok let’s eat some chocolate, “oh no its poison maid get me charcoal”, maid wasn’t quick enough and I died.
- Let’s go to that party, get ambushed and shot with an arrow, “I think your meant to pull it out”, dies.
And so will yours when you start, but as you play you can get the gist fairly easily of how to balance lessons and mood to improve skills quickly. This will help in training needed skills and lead to some better success at certain tests.
The thing that puts people off this game though is the random skills checks that make it up, as almost everything you do is based on a skill or effects your mood. It is impossible to commit every option to memory, your better writing them down. This means if you leave the game for a while you will likely forget what skills are important throughout the early game, as I did myself. This can get frustrating but that’s just how it is and learning all the skill checks isn’t easy.
Overall I find this game fun to come back to and see how far I can succeed in ruling my kingdom, the artwork is lovely, and the outfits you get after reaching certain skill sets are a nice aesthetic touch. If you enjoy exploring the lore of the world and Elodie’s family ties, along with lovely artwork and a fair bit of micromanaging and learning challenges, I would highly recommend it. It is a great and replayable game, with many different routes you can take on your way to becoming queen.
Just remember though her name is Elo’die’

I think this best way to sum up this game would be to simply called it "pocket/mini sized strategy."
Starships comes at a weird time Firaxis and 2K games.  Beyond Earth left many consumers wanting more and genuinely confused.  Why did they charge for a full price game that amounted to nothing more than an expansion pack for Civ 5?   SO what do they do?  They make a game even smaller in scale than BE and charge much less for it.  I assume the strategy now is: "the price should match the experience" and what you get with Starships pretty much feels like a $15 game.
I'll get this out of the way immediately: this is a mobile game that happens to playable on the PC.  What does that mean?  Well, it means that a lot of the complexity of the Civ series is stripped out and the player is left to make spot decisions and map movement choices.  The interface was clearly designed for tablet touchscreen.  The buttons are in weird places and the menus/screens are stripped to the bar bones essentials.  That said, there is an enjoyable strategy game to be played here.  Let's take a moment to talk about it...
The gameplay:
Players familiar with Civ 5 will immediately recognize the hex grid format.  The player starts on the grid with a small fleet of starships and a planet.  Each "turn" basically boils down to this pattern:
- Spend Resources on starships, planets and various upgrades
- Move your war fleet to a new planet
- Complete the mission on that planet (aka combat, more on this in a moment), thus gaining influence over that planet
- MAYBE move again and do a new mission on a different planet
- End Turn (aka Shore Leave)
Let me touch on the combat scenarios (missions) on each planet:
When the players arrives on a new planet that isn't already in their empire, the citizens of the planet will request help in the form of some type of starship mission.  This is where the real strategy of the game comes into play and the theme of "starships" really plays out.  Whatever war fleet the player has assembled is now used in a turn based mini strategy game.  It is important to note that SOMETIMES the mission doesn't use the player's war fleet but instead presents some type of puzzle.  But most (>70%) of the time the player must use his/her forces to defeat a squadron of NPC starships.
The battle scenarios are most similar to "war" in Civ 5.  Each mission is played on its own hex map (separate from the overworld map) where the player manuevers their starships and fires various weapons to destroy the enemy NPCs.    Each starship is its own character on the map so if the player has five starships in their fleet, they now can battle with five ships on the combat map. This is defintely the BEST part of the game.  This is where all the time spent buying new ships and upgrading them pays off.  The player can choose to stay back and use long range weapons to try and get up close and personal with fighters or close range weapons.  If the player is successful, they "win" influence over the planet and eventually it folds into their empire.
The players wins the entire game when they control most of the overworld map (or lose if they fail to do so).  I *think* its 70%. (Update: There are several victory conditions present but in my play time, so far, I have usually won by accidentally acquiriing 70% of the map.)  When playing on easy mode it is very easy.  Medium and Hard present much better challenges.
The truth is that the game isn't very deep.  Upgrading planets and ships usually involves just buying everything.  There aren't really any penalties or drawbacks.  Even if the player concentrates on, for example, energy production, eventually it all evens out.  And that's where Starships is arguably very weak.  This is not a deep game.  The best part of the game is the combat and the starships.  Everything else is nothing much more than a big map the player simply uses to move and drive the game.
I found the $15 is worth it.  The strategy of the starship combat is fun albeit not engaging.  The game does retain the "one more turn" type gameplay but that's where it ends.  The overall, 4x strategy simply isn't present.
Bottom line?
This is a $15 strategy game and I recommend it based on the starship combat.  If you want a bigger strategy, with more depth, look somewhere else.
Final Score: C

This game is absolutely amazing not just to me but for others in my family too. My father used to be a gamer himself back in the days of the atari followed by nintendo days as well. He was also my gaming buddy during those days. After the nes/snes days however, he kind of gave up on gaming as a hobby because he said he did not feel the magic in the kind of games that were being made on the pc/ps2/xbox etc.
Fast forward to 2014 or thereabouts which is when I discovers dark souls and introduce him to it as well and this is one action game that did love.
He said he felt the same kind of magic in this game (and Portal/Portal2) which he had felt in his early days of gaming on the atari/nes and I having experienced those games myself I have to agree. While being a modern game, dark souls does do a lot of things in the style of older games and this is one of the things which makes it endearing to so many people I guess.
I have also introduced non gamers to these games and even they could immediately see that this game is something artistic and different (in a good way) from most AAA trash that floats around in the world of gaming these days. The sense of being in a once magnificient but dying world is so beuatifully communicated to you by everything from the visuals, music and even the excellent combat that its easy to get lost in this world.
I have had so much fun playing this game the last few years both alone and with friends and family and its something that I recommend every gamer at least try to do. I know that this its not a great PC port but using a controller and simple ini file mod like dsfix solves most of the issues it has. Then there is another mod DSCM which makes the multiplayer come alive.
The final hurdle you might have before you can dive in and enjoy this gem of a world is that this game has slower more deliberate combat compared to any hack-n-slash game you might have played. On top of that, a lot of the ingame stats and systems are never explained to you for which I recommend you read one of the many brilliant starter guides for this game. Oh and after you finish the game (or even before that) be sure to go on youtube and watch some of the lore videos for dark souls 1 especially from a creator called vatividya. I guarantee that you will find yourself shedding a tear or two on several of those videos...

TL;DR: a lovely game I find difficult to recommend.
In a nutshell, Long Live the Queen is a visual novel style, stat min-maxing, groundhog day simulator (or would it be a groundhog year simulator?). You play as princess-queen Elodie, crowned dangerously young after her mother's death, who has to run her kingdom by picking from a handful of choices each week. Her choices and outcomes come from passing skill checks, and are otherwise based on what Elodie learned and chose previously. Things start to become complicated at this point -- all her choices are basically intertwined. Choices affect Elodie's mood, which affects how quickly she studies different subjects. Typically, Elodie and her kingdom end up hosed, so you're going to be restarting a lot. It's a compelling game that keeps you doggedly restarting to see if, this time, you can secure Elodie her throne and unravel the conspiracies and mysteries surrounding her. However, I feel it has deep flaws in its gameplay loop.
At face value, the game's core goal is to spend Elodie's time efficiently to level up the right skills to survive an onslaught of skill checks, but that summary's not quite there yet. Each playthrough lasts a brief 40 turns / weeks, there are plenty of ways to get offed, and it's almost impossible to have enough skill points to pass every skill check, so you have to choose a small handful of skills. For example, there are over five different skills that Elodie uses to gain information about her surroundings, and since relatively high skill checks come in play during the first half of the game, I don't think you can figure out all the intrigue in a single playthrough, let alone do it and get a happy ending. This game requires multiple playthroughs to find a way to the end naturally, and even more playthroughs to learn everything or get your desired ending. A better explanation of core of the game would be to, over multiple playthroughs, build up one of several optimized solutions to the skill check puzzles of the game. But that's not quite right either.
It's not right because it doesn't capture how many little tidbits of information you have to tease out of the game. Really, this game is about learning which skill checks are important to survival (and your desired ending), how high the skill checks are, and which skill checks and mood changes will come in the future from taking certain actions. If you're going for your desired ending, it's also about figuring out the hidden stats, like Lumen approval, Cruelty, how many soldiers you have and how much money you have. Figuring out all of this information without going to the wiki is a trial-and-error nightmare, which is where my complaints start to come in:
- It's Groundhog year, but the game won't remember anything for you: The game doesn't organize information from previous runs for the player, and it's not easy to remember. (I'm not expecting Elodie to know things just because she knew them on a previous playthrough). There's no map of the surrounding territories. There are no family trees. Minor characters often don't have pictures. Dialogue choices don't show what mood changes will result. For instance, I remember that visiting Charlotte in week 1 will cheer me up, but I can't remember what visiting dad will do. Even though I've done it before, the game wont show me. I wish it would -- I need some way to remind myself of what's going on, since it's so easy to forget little details from ten minutes ago while juggling stat management and new lore. I'd rather not transcribe things like "In the year 950, king whatzisface slayed baron hoozdat over the death of his son datboi" over and over again, or things like "week 1: speaking to king makes Elodie sad". The game pushes me to rely on the wiki.
- Figuring out flags, checks, and hidden stats is hard: This is a similar complaint, but focused on the stats side. Firstly, even though the game does make savescumming a little easy by allowing tons of saves, it's still kind of awkward. I think the auto saves allow you to rewind back to any day, but they're not labelled at all. Secondly, while the game tries to show you what's causing events to happen showing you when you encounter skill checks, the game doesn't show you how high the checks are (and they're not at even multiples of 25, so it's not easy to guess). Thirdly, although the game is willing to show you when it checks for skills, it won't show you when it checks for flags. Fourthly, If you don't have an option, it won't be greyed out -- it'll be missing. Fifthly, there are hidden stats in the game which important for the ending, such as nobility approval. All of these five combine to make figuring out how to get endings brutal, since I'd essentially have to make a few runs dedicated to figuring out each stat check. Of course, I could always just rely on the wiki.
Don't get me wrong -- I love games where I feel a compulsion to map things out, write things down, and unravel mysteries. But this game is too frustrating and keeps pushing me to the wiki. I'm basically being given a choice between three options:
A): flail around in the darkness without really thinking things through
B): run through the game a million times to know for certain what the numbers behind the game actually are
C): look at the wiki and work from there
C is basically the most sane option. But I don't want to look at the wiki. The wiki is disorganized, it's full of spoilers, and reading it makes me feel like I'm cheating. On top of that, I'm a firm believer in games being enjoyable, challenging, and masterable without the need for guides on principle.

Never played a Type-Moon game before, so this was my first introduction to the Fate series. I seriously don't see how anyone couldn't follow the plot or that it was hard to understand what was going on because they weren't a fan of the series... sure it makes reference to past games, and I think maybe the anime, and the characters are mostly past entries in this series, but the plot of this game is not really a continuation, it's just based in the Fate universe with it taking place after Fate/Extra. You can play this as a standalone game and enjoy what it has to offer. I adored the characters, and I thought the plot in terms of the relationship dynamics was executed wonderfully.
The gameplay itself is inspired by the Musou series of games (Dynasty Warriors, Samurai Warriors, Warriors Orochi), and it does a great job of adding enough original ideas mixed with that style to feel like it's own thing. There could be some improvements, and hopefully, the sequel will fix that, but as hack and slash, 1 vs 1000 game, it does it's job well, and me being a Musou game fan, I loved it. It also doubles as a visual novel/dating type of game too, as you bond with the characters you play as. I like this idea over the Koei Tecmo games because it adds a more human element to the characters you control, I care for the character I play as because I've befriended them and bonded with them through my interactions with them. I just wish there was more than the three charcaters that you could have this interaction with, because I would love to have that same level of interaction with a character like Artoria Pendragon or Elizabeth Bathory, something which again I hope they improve in the sequel.
Other than that. Great game. If you like Dynasty Warriors and the various spin-offs (Like Hyrule Warriors and/or Fire Emblem Warriors) you'll probably love this, and with the added visual novel feel with the "dating" elements it's probably gonna appeal to the "waifu/husbando" lovers out there. And this game is certainly well suited on the Nintendo Switch with the fact that you can take this anywhere and enjoy hack and slash action on the go and on a big TV. Can't wait for the sequel!

Zone traps are a terrible mechanic, only coming into play to hurt the player.  If I could throw cu chulainn into zones to trigger traps, he'd finally be useful to me. This review is from an old school 80s kid who grew up with Nintendo and Genesis games...
This game is an excellent 2d ARPG. Yes, one could describe it as a Zelda Clone, but that shouldn't be taken as a negative.
You play as a boy trying to find his father, or something like that. You gain magic spells that can be used to solve puzzles and fight monsters. Instead of weapons, you use spells to dispatch enemies.
The game plays just like a top down Zelda would: you have a overworld that you can explore and find treasture; you find items that expand your abilities and allow you to progress further into the game; there are dungeons that test your physical prowess and mental ability; and the fighting is done in real time. There's a story tacked on, but it's not very good or engrossing.
I really enjoyed playing the game because the puzzles are nice brain teasers and the game is easy to pick up and play in short bursts or long sessions. Finding hidden items is never boring and there's always something new to discover. Also, you learn new spells that keeps the action fresh and entertaining.
System wise: there are no options for resolution or graphical effects. However, I did not have any problem running the game and it looks like it was running at 1080p. The sprites are colorful and the animation, although not amazingly dynamic, looks fine and suits this type of game.

You progress through the game and the main story by fighting and taking over sectors of the Moon Cell and battling servants in those sectors. But the thing is, is that there is a lot of going back and forth through the sectors since some mob's can invade sectors that you've taken over so you have to go back and take them back again and kill the mob's that can invade your sectors, personally I think this was a move to expand the game time by a large amount, but I wouldn't say that it wasn't a bad move since personally I very much so enjoyed going back and taking them back again. The story itself isn't that interesting or crazy during the Nero route its just you and Nero (who very much so provides a lot of fan service and is pretty much in love with you) trying to find out why is the other half of you is with Tomoe no mae and essentially trying to get that other half back since you don't feel whole, its not a very, serious story but its a fun one.

For this reason alone I enjoy the game. It is a simple strategy game I can run through in a couple hours. I did nto expect deep immersion or heavy strategy. The AI is  weak but I have not tried larger maps or more difficult play levels (played on normal).  I do see how this game could be quite nasty between human players! A live opponent won;t let you suck up too many planets and will not fall hopelessly behind technologically. He will also react to any min/maxing you do.
Strategic play is simple you get 3-4 'moves' with your fleet. In each move you can attempt to complete a mission to win influence over a neutral planet or attack an opponents. You an build tech, cities, wonders, or buildings on planets. They tend to boost production ot in the case of wonders provide a serious boost to a ship system. The game does not have the wonder race you expect from Civ so no frustrating waste of many turns of resources only to be beat to the unique wonder.
Tactically you move around a small map with various debris. There are some advantages to position (back shots hit weaker shields without the smart shield wonder) Lasers are long range and lose less damage though asteroids while plasmas are short range and lose more damage through terrain. Torpedoes are fired on fixed vector and can exploded any time after the first turn. They rarely hit but do force the enemy to move out their way which can allow you to split a larger fleet up. Fighters are an excellent way to extend damage and potentially draw enemy fire from main ships.
So in closing if you are looking for Civ5 in space don;t buy this. If you want a fun little strat game to burn some time I recomment it. If you have a few friends you want to trounce I highly recommend it.

State of Decay Assassin's Creed came out in 2013 and  it still looks good for its age and badly optimized engine.
I got the first game with full price and the rest on sale, it was definitely worth it. But if you are considering buying this game, buy YOSE edition, it will have better graphics and a few fixes.  I will be giving a review for State of decay itself and its DLCs.
So lets move on to where is the fun of this game in general.  It is 3D zombie survival simulator with elements of RPG. You get yourself and your team, who have random characteristics and skills. You get to do almost everything you can imagine you would actually do in the situation of being a human in zombie apocalypse.  Scavenging, saving people, exploring and so on. The fun comes with all of it combined together in a single game.
Controls. This game was ported from xbox I believe, so the controls are a bit weird, but its totally cool. You just need to remember what to push when things happen. It gets weird thou when you have to use special skills or combos.
While playing this game you don't often notice the sound effects and the music, but I can tell that it plays its part in delivering the whole picture very well. Its nothing impressive, but what is important that it does not spoil the experience and only enchants it. Although I have not tried, but I can see myself actually playing some other music while running around the city.
I bought the game in 2013 and sadly my PC couldnt run it on the good settings. Sadly as I find out now, the graphics difference is very small. So playing on min settings wont bother you that much. Graphics themselves are pretty good. They deliver what you need to experience very good. I would encourage more fog though just so that you cant see that clearly. Also there is only fine weather, meaning you wont get any rain. Even though the game has a day and night cycle so its not too bad.
And the bads, lets see, there are plenty of bugs, I only got to see a few of them, but they are moldy annoying. There are no fixes, so you get what you get. There is also not enough interaction with other members of your group. Missions are very limited by the script. Glitchy as it is,  the game is still good and worth playing and paying for.
The story is not the only thing you can do in this game even if you dont purchase the DLCs. But I do encourage you that you buy them nonetheless. The story itself is kinda crap. It pretty much just lets you know what is going on in the world.
The second DLC Breakdown is an infinite survival game (unless you die) with every level of it much harder. This is what I am mostly playing. Once you level up you start from the scratch ( but you get a team and resources) . Very fun and challenging, which I like a lot. The game will make you think if you want to do a loud move because in doing so you may actually get absolutely destroyed. And the last DLC Lifeline tells you a story of the Army in the city. It has special missions, new characters and other stuff, but I didnt find it as entertaining.
Re-playability is very high in my opinion, because you can do so many things in a different ways that you just want to keep trying until you figure out the perfect combo for everything.
So in overall, I think the developers made a externally good game even though it has a couple of DLCs and a remade version of it. I would recommend this game to pretty much anybody. If you spend 6 hours into the game then you have used the money in the right way.

Negatives:
-People often float everywhere and the animations are busted.

-Combat system is all about awkward animations and clicking.
I get the feeling that the developers made the game so that they would enjoy it, and not so that we would enjoy it:
-There are loads of systems at play which are mega-confusing to anyone except the people who made the game or have the time to read through lengthy guides online. It doesn't help that the game doesn't pause when you're in the menus, so you can't even take your time to study them or learn what's going on. Every couple of seconds there's someone shouting over the radio or a zombie approaching - I like that they were trying to emulate the experience of the zombie apocalypse, but I'm trying to learn the damn menus and read the damn numbers and remember what I was doing last time I played. And that leads onto the next problem:
-You have to download a mod to turn off the 'feature' where medical supplies/food/etc are used up in real time when you're not playing the game (the worst design decision I have ever seen). If you stop playing for a while, loads of your supplies are used up. Not because anyone in the game world did anything, but because you yourself stopped playing the game for a week. Makes no sense whatsoever.
Positives:
-You can't buy this.

If Telltale's Walking Dead games spend their time dissecting the human element of life after catastrophe, then State of Decay spends its time focussing on the logistics and struggle within the world itself. The mechanical challenge of scavenging for supplies, moving from spot to spot as resources grow scarce, and of course killing zombies is absorbing and a lot of fun.
It's a shame that the finer details of the game don't hold up though. Dialogue is often quite stilted, mission structure is repetitive, the story is bland, and the artificial intelligence is too stupid to live. At one point I watched zombies burst in through the front door of an AI settlement, only to be ignored by all but one of the people wandering around inside. One man in body armor leaned against a wall and ate an apple while an NPC grappled with the undead not five feet away from him. Oh, and the cars obey no known laws of physics.
On the whole State of Decay is still worth playing. It's satisfying to watch your little community grow, and to crack some skulls along the way.

Have you ever dreamed of a game that is a mix of minecraft, total war, FPS action, with some pirateering thrown in for good measure? If so, this game is for you. In From the Depths, build a ship (or fleet of ships) in order to wipe out the opposing factions. You do this by capturing resource zones where you can drill for resources to build bigger better ships. This simple goal leads to a very open experiance. The map/planet of Nieter alone has about seven or so factions to interact with through a simple to understand diplomacy panel, a massive amount of space to conquer, with some islands sprinkled in to use however you like. That's not even mentioning the built in planet builder, where you get to create a whole new experiance, or the planets that the developer is probably planning to patch in. The planet itself is not whats interesting however. Its the ship building. You have a very wide range of blocks, each with different functions to build your fleet with. You can build everything from massive steel battleships, to wooden sail based gallions, to riverboat paddlesteamers. If you find that you dont like building ships, you can board and take over the enemy ships. You could say "Screw sailing" and build an airship if you so choose. You can costomize every aspect of your ship, even the guns/lazers/kim jong un approved missiles it carries. I definitely think that this game is worth the money. FAIR WARNING: This game is fairly difficult to learn. Be prepared to do some resarch/ watch some youtube videos.

This is an early access review and I will update it should I return to Warstone once it is finalized.  It is also strictly from a stand-alone single player point of view.
This is a long-term grinder with a lengthy single-player campaign and online PvP/Coop game-play.  Depending on the mission, the placement of towers can be static (i.e. pre-defined) spots or it can be free-form (i.e. build a maze).
I quit playing after I decided that the free-form building was still in need of signifigant work.  The tower placement points seem 'leaky' and different waves will sometimes conform to the maze you have built while other waves will slip between towers.  I have zero time for that kind of nonsense.
I also don't like that tower placement points are unknown until a given wave is completed - tower placement points 'appear' at the end of waves, forcing you to review the map and make tower build decisions without a lot of time to consider.  Sometimes you miss seeing the build point since they do absolutely nothing to draw attention to their unannounced availability.
How hard would it be to mark all of the placement points at the start of a mission - and then put the number of a wave inside the box?  You would then be able to plan - save your funds so you can take advantage of new tower points instead of being broke from having done a few upgrades.
I did not engage in the online modes nor are they important to me.  I suspect that I would heap more praise on the game if it were a factor.

¡I played this game for about 35 minutes and i have to say i enjoyed it quite a lot, so i'll make a honest review of it!
Basically, it is a very good TRIBUTE to Blaster Master using a lot of it's design choices and taking some alternate routes to modernize and make the game more accesible for new generations, the developer has made it clear that it is a tribute, and a pretty good one, i have to say.
Graphics: The graphics are not bad, but they could use some polish, especially in the textures department. I understand the game goes for a retro inspired look, but even Blaster Master had gorgeous graphics for it's time, perhaps the developer could try to mimic these textures, that would be appreciated in future updates.
Music: I didn't find the music to be bad, not good either, it is not the strongest aspect of the game, but i haven't found a song that became tiresome... It could be a lot more memorable though (Like the original game's soundtrack)
Gameplay: The part i liked the most is the gameplay, and what a shame it is that a lot of people could put down this game solely based on the reviews i've read. Guys, sincerely i had fun, it is an enjoyable experience, the platforming is entertaining (especially after you get some of the upgrades) and the changes in gameplay style (the game offers a sidescrolling and 3d tank view, and the same for the human driving it.) are a welcome breath of fresh air. I never encountered a part where the gameplay was a bother (some jumps are harder than others, but i saw that in Blaster Master too!).
What i liked:
+ Mantains the retro style gameplay, the challenge, the feeling of loneliness and the mystery of the original game.
+ Expands on these concepts with new ideas, 3d enviroments and responsive controls
+ The developer put the Hover ability (a very useful one that you used to get in the final half of the game) almost at the start, which for me is a big plus, because i love it and it makes the game a lot more enjoyable.
What i DIDN'T like:
- The textures are not appealing, the enviroments look a little bit dull.
. A minor complain: The enemies have no animations, they just jump/shoot at you (I think this was a choice made to mimic the original enemies in Blaster Master, but i think that it looks a little bit... awkward and overly simple.
- The music (which was a BIG part of Blaster Master) is not memorable at all, sorry, but it could use a big overhaul.
- I would have loved to play at a higher resolution, or remap the keys, which at the current version, is not possible.
- I loved the story of Blaster Master, i think the story could be a stronger part of this game too.
- The bosses of the original game where amazing, in Helena the 3rd, i couldn't find any boss fight at all, and i think that's one of the achilles heels of the game. It was very dissapointing to be honest.
I didn't fell through the floor, maybe it was pure luck, i've read reviews of people that had this issue, so i hope it is promptly fixed. BUT i did found a game-breaking glitch... The hover ability is bugged, absolutely broken. I won't say how, because that would RUIN the experience for other players. I found a way to refill the hover everytime i pressed a button, so PLEASE, PLEASE fix that! I could get to places i shouldn't have because of this issue, and in a Metroidvania game this is fatal! (If the developer wants more information about this, feel free to contact me, i will give all the details about this bug)
Overall, for 5 bucks (i got this game even cheaper in an indiegala bundle so check that out!) the game is awesome for the price, i loved it and would like to see updates to it, i consider myself a fan of the original Blaster Master, and this game almost hits the notes, so keep up the good work guys!

I bought this because I was a fan of the old NES game Blaster Master and this looked like a new version of that.
From what I can tell I personally think it was worth my 5 dollars.
You get 3 gameplay styles; the side scroller inside the tank, a FPS style inside the tank, and a FPS shooter as a human outside of the tank.
I didn't get far enough to see if there was any use for the human mode in the 2d side scroller, so that might come in later.
The controls were easy for me. I used the gamepad which used one joystick for moving, one for aiming, one trigger for jumping, and one trigger for shooting.
The depth perception in the 3D mode while jumping is a little tricky since you sometimes need to jump up or down and the camera didn't help much with that, so sometimes it was just a jump and hope you land in the right spot.
The A.I. enemies are very basic, they run straight for you and if they touch you it hurts. The first enemies can only jump, but some enemies can shoot soon after.
Overall, I enjoyed the 30 minutes or so I played to test the game out, and I plan to play more in the future to see all the cool upgrades the tank gets, and different guns the human gets.
For my money, I'd give this game a 8/10 for price and enjoyment.

I have read a number of reviews that have already been posted here.  I understand why there's a lot of mixed feelings about the game, that's to be expected when you slap Sid Meier's name on something.  Many came expecting a deeper game, albiet not as deep as a full-on Civ.  Others came expecting more choices and options.  My main gripe is the lack of the everpresent tooltips we've come to rely on in other Sid Meier games.
That said...this game is awesome.  If you're looking for a quick, fun, tired-as-hell-after-work-all-day game, this is it.  Games can be a fast 2-3 hrs, or you can drag it out on very hard difficulties for a nice weekender puzzle.
I'd have liked more fleet management complexity.  For example the automatic ship class upgrades.  I'd have preferred to have a choice of hulls and paid more or less to have bigger or larger hulls.  Smaller hulls having a maximum upgrade level or some such.  I'd have liked being able to split my fleet into 2 or more fleets, especially as controlled space got larger and harder to defend.
The diplomacy is a little weird.  I tried to figure out how to form an alliance with someone, and there's....nothing.  It just somehow *happened* anyway as the game went on.  I found myself at war with an empire I'd only just discovered, and there was no way to end it diplomatically.  I had to just waltz in and annihilate them to get it over with.
Research is almost pointless.  Even with getting tech as fast as I could via research points, I had only a couple techs to level 2 (of 8?) by the end of the game.  Grab what techs you want/can, and move on.  Your fleet's upgrades are much more important.
Also, once you've collected a few specific combinations of wonders, your fleet becomes virtually invincible.  I had extra actions, auto-stealth, and a couple others that made my shields invulnerable to lasers and torpedos...toss up a fighter screen in the first turn, and the enemy will NEVER see your ships, and waste themselves on your massive fighter screen.
All-in-all a good game, but there are places where they clearly oversimplified it.  It could have been more complex and engaging and still been a hit for PC as well as tablets.

Sci-Fi Digital Strategy Board Game
( I had to sit down with the game for a number of hours before coming up with the exact reasons why I enjoy it, and it very much earns it's positive recommendation. I'll probably edit this again)
It's all about enjoying a digital board game set in space and chilling out. This is a lite-tactical hexagonal space mission game. As captain of a federation, you are charged with bouncing the fleet between planets completing various types of missions and winning over the galaxy that resulted in the wake of Beyond Earth. From the rewards from victories and accumulated resources, you're able to upgrade your ships in a few different ways from increasing their basic health and strength to providing abilities like stealth, torpedo salvos and carrier-borne interceptors. Strategic diplomacy is extremely basic, and amounts to whether you want to deal with the AI directly opposing you or not.
The game is very simple, and I recommend watching a "Let's Play" on YouTube before buying as it's a large departure from Firaxis' other games. The game feels like it'd be at home on a tablet or phone due to it's simplicity.
The gameplay pacing is well suited for short stints for people that want to relax with a small space tactical game. I think it's great to do a full voyage (about 4 missions) and then put the game down for a bit. It's not for great hour long marathons, but a full game might take anywhere from 1-2 hours.
So does it reflect Firaxis' Civ "just one more turn" philosophy? Probably not. But is that really a bad thing? It depends on what you were looking for. It's great for those times when one is juggling other tasks.
There are very few areas where I'd nit-pick it, especially as a single player game. There are many player strategies which are very unbalanced, such as cloaking mixed with some of the Wonders. I would say that the most fun I have is when I pick it up with a particular house-rule for my gameplay that restricts a particular technology or strategy that I'd used prior.
I would love to see the ability to mod in and out various aspects, such as to revamp the resources in a drawn out game, and more of the missions reminicent of the exploration phase.
From a technical perspective, if this was done in Ruby, I'm impressed and hopeful.
I think it'd be a great project for even a scripter or programmer to step in and change things to suit their own tastes.

Ah, State of Decay.  You are a cruel mistress.  You dangle characters and story arcs in front of us, potential for characters to grow, but one slip-up, one false move, and that character you spent hours and hours building?  Dead.  Gone. After many years of owning this game I think I can finally sit down and write a review about it.
Starbound is wonderful, it brings together many different concepts and genres into one spectacular game. Sentient Novas that are Cowboys? Yes. Medieval Robots? Yes. Gorilla People? Yes. Frogmen with Fezzes? YES. I am not a big fan of Genre mashing, but the way Chucklefish does it is great.
Of course the main theme of the game is Sci-Fi Exploration and Construction, which I would like to point out is excellently crafted and extremely fun to play, especially in a 2D platform kind of way.
I believe the only con I MIGHT give this game is that some players may find it to be grindy, but in my opinion I can't find it to be that bad. Chucklefish have found a way to make it fun by sprinkleing dozens of small (and large) dungeons for players to find and explore, as well as many civilizations to trade with, or conquer if your into that kinda thing.
When you purchase this game, load it up for the first time, you will truly see how vast and expansive it really is. You wont stop playing until Twelve hours later when you realize how damn fun (and Time consuming) it is!

To be honest,the game is good all around,the characters are nice,the animation is nice,the weapons are nice too,but the story, It gets very repetitive after EITHER you have done about 2-3 quests for clues,or played through the entire story twice.
I can explain the entire game in a few sentences. And here i go.
Attend some ceremony,escape earth,go see this old lady,fetch some crystals,find Floran things,fight a boss,find Hylotl things,fight a boss,find Avian things,fight a boss,find Apex things,fight a boss,find Glitch things,fight a boss,open a big gate,kill a big boss,THE END,go play something new.
As you can see by that it's quite repetitive. It WOULD make it nicer if each of the races had unique stories,but i think that would mess up mods that add modded races. The pinnacle of the entire game is,in my opinion,exploring the universe after the game ends. You are free to do anything you please,and you are not forced to gear up and fight some bosses. It's also like No Man's Sky but about infinitely better and alot cheaper. If you're planning to buy No Man's Sky you should seriously consider buying Starbound instead. All in all it's a nice game,but repetitive,and the ending wasn't that sad,in fact,it doesn't have all that much substance. I feel that this could have been WAY more sucessful if we weren't exploring planet after planet and wasting fuel just to find some clues for most of the game,sure,maybe you'd get better gear or complete quests for rewards during the quests for the clues,but they are quite boring. And after you complete the game once you know that you'll need to sit through all of that again just to move on and complete the game. Also the bosses DO drop cool weapons,but they drop almost never,there's mods to fix that however. Also i'm pretty sure that without a workshop and good mods that are available for starbound about half of the fun would be gone,i hope this review helped you understand the game better.

Once upon a time when the Gamecube came out I was on the youngish side. I was looking for a game to play and I was recommended by the store clerk to try Tales of Symphonia because he knew I liked rpgs.
Right from the beginning I was drawn into the world and the storyline. These characters became a better part of my gaming childhood I suppose. I put so many hours into it, worked every quest to completion, every side boss and storyline. I burned through two copies of the game.
And then time wore on and I packed my Gamecube away for other consoles, but Tales of Symphonia always had a special place in my heart as my favourite game.
It was released on Playstation 3: not my console of choice but I was still grabby hands at the collectors edition and sat down once more to play through the game. It still hadn't lost it's magic and again I played the game until I lost my charger for my controllers and I couldn't find a replacement so I put it away.
And then lo and behold it was finally released for pc, the port was awful at first so I held off on buying it, but I was watching, waiting until it was patched and soon as I was able I picked it up and I've just started replaying it.
Tales of Symphonia for me is timeless, it's one of those games I can pick up and play over and over and over and it never loses it's magic. This game was a big part of my life as a youngling and seeing it here and being able to play it on my pc makes me really happy. It should've been ported a long time ago, better too because it's a game that anyone can love. You find yourself drawn into the struggles and stories of the characters and the overarching plotline. The graphics might be old, but the music and gameplay carry it well, even years later.
I've always enjoyed the combat system of the Tales series and Symphonia is no exception, though I do confess I needed to rebind a few keys it wasn't the most friendly of set ups but once you get the hang of it it's pretty easy to waltz through the battles or make it a challenge for yourself.
Either way, for someone who has played this game for hours upon hours, who bawled her eyes out when the opening music started playing, this is a game that will worm it's way into your heart with a fondness that you'll carry with you for years to come.

Warning: I'm approaching this game as a fan of the series. Anyways I'm trying to review objectively.
Fate/Extella is a JRPG Hack Slash game with two features defining it... a) Grinding like battles b) Visual Novel elements
So first of all I recommend you liking at least 1 of those 2 if you're intending to buy the game.
From the beginning you get a lot of storytelling, with great narrative, summing up a good story, afterwards you get to meet a lot of the characters known in the franchise. The battle element of the game is a lot of Hack and Slash grinding, fighting over domains, against enemy mobs and servants. Your own NPC servants and mobs defend your territories as you go around fighting and i'd say it's just OK as it gets somehow tedious when you're trying the same stage for the 3rd time (maybe i wasn't good enough senpai!).
Pros
- Great story, with narrative reminding us of the classic Fate Visual Novels.
- There's a good ammount of the Fate franchise characters. (Check cons)
- Voice acting is always good in this kinda games!
- Gallery for you to check on the game scenes, characters, items and etc.
- The soundtrack is compelling and you can check it on the library
Cons
- The fighting can get a bit tiresome after a few battles.
- Only 3 of all the characters are main so you'll mainly be playing with those at first.
- The keyboard layout is just weird for me, using a controller works totally fine.
If you like JRPG's, visual novels or the Fate franchise please, check this game out and enjoy, otherwise please read carefully and check some gameplay videos... or wait a while for better discounts.
Overall Rating 70/100

Luftrausers is a fun little game. The game feel is excellent, the aesthetic and general presentation is well put together, and the game mechanics are clever, simple, and engaging (see the Steam video to understand all you need to know). Unfortunately, the game's progression, while paced well, is quickly plateaued. Within an hour or so, you should unlock most of the unlockable parts. This isn't bad in and of itself, but after this, there isn't much incentive to continue except the high score. The UI is also pretty awkward and clunky, with virtually no options, and poor gamepad support.

If you like like shooting for high scores, by all means, you may very well spend hours in this game. But for people who don't, this may feel a little too empty to warrant a full price purchase.

So far, I'm really enjoying Warstone. I've played similar games before, such as Defender's Quest and Kingdom Rush, and whilst Warstone is somewhat similar, it is refreshingly different in many ways.
The storyline is quite amusing, and there is a variety of fun level modes over the course of the game. Unlike most TD games, this one is multiplayer, with the option of going co-op or PVP. These levels are seperate from the main storyline so they don't hinder your progression.
If you aren't a fan of the city-building, you can turn it off (however, this does mean turning off the story too). I've been playing with it on, and I'm a little bit stuck grinding earlier levels on higher difficulties for wood and stone so I can complete quests/upgrades and progress further in the game. It is early access - meaning that there are some bugs that have to be ironed out. The game also requires a constant internet connection due to the multiplayer feature, but it isn't something I've had any problems with.
I got the game on sale (£6.29 instead of £9.99), but I feel like the game is worth full price. Whether you are a newcomer or veteran to the TD genre, Warstone will be a great addition to your steam library.

Starbound is wonderful, it brings together many different concepts and genres into one spectacular game. Sentient Novas that are Cowboys? Yes. Medieval Robots? Yes. Gorilla People? Yes. Frogmen with Fezzes? YES. I am not a big fan of Genre mashing, but the way Chucklefish does it is great.

Dark Souls is a bona-fide classic videogame, but it is not for the casual player, feint of heart, or those lacking in willpower  and perseverance - in fact it is a real test of the latter. Getting to the end will be quite the ordeal and the experience.
It hearkens back to early computer RPG games that were often brutally hard, or sometimes unfair - when games were actual games - not interactive movies - and playing it did not guarantee that you'd ever reach the end without some real skill.
It is an action role-playing game in a beatiful and artfully rendered fantasy world. The game design is actually brilliant. You will see those secrets you can't reach (yet), and vistas from yonder that you can't yet travel to.... and in many other games you wouldn't be able to - it would just be background.... but Dark Souls is different.
In trying to explore the landscape, you will die.... a lot... from all manner of deadly and frightening things. For all players this is a necessary sacrifice and the game treats it as such. There are things that this game wants to teach you, but it is not spelled out for you, and each scene is left as a vague puzzle for the player to solve. Secrets abound, and the game does not give them up easily. Just figuring out the game's backstory is half the fun, and how it ties into the world you are exploring. Visual clues in the environment tell the story without ever saying anything - if you've been paying attention. All things in this game are not what they seem.
The fighting mechanics are often a puzzle in themselves. The battles feel weighty, and as long as you remember to lock-on to targets appropriately - are fun and satisfying.
The boss fights will leave you blown away... visually and literally. For the most part they are huge behemoths, and look eerily frightening in a way most boss battles in most other games do not. The game oozes atmosphere.
When you realize that your player is "undead" and you truly cannot ever get stuck and "lose" the game, then the game begins to open up. You're only truly staying dead if you choose to. Winning then, becomes an exercise in the aforementioned perseverence, overcoming hundreds of deaths that are certainly coming your way. The good news is that the game keeps driving you forward, and providing strange and wonderful new vistas to explore so you will want to see them all - and usually die trying.
The difficulty of this game is an incredible illusion. Let's just leave it at that. There is more than one way to play. More than one way to complete the game. Some easier than others. Some deceptively so. None of it is really explained. The brilliant game design allows for all manner of attempts. It will leave your head scratching like a good puzzle game should - but Dark Souls doesn't look like a puzzle game at all.
Dark Souls will leave it's mark on you - long after you've finished playing. In fact you just may not want to finish playing. There's an online world of battles get involved in.... but only if you restore your humanity. The question is.... will you lose it playing this game or will you find it? Will your suffering pave the way to personal glory over an undead world, or acceptance and readiness to sacrifice?
If you enjoy being angry and not having fun, play this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game ^_^

My sister never stopped playing that game, the story is fascinating, and I love the characters of the game including Lloyd, Genis, Kratos, Zelos, Yuan, Colette and so on. It never gets any old, but just a few years later, I played the Knight of Ratatosk, the second part of Tales of symphonia, the story goes on, but somehow it feels too random, but I still love the first part.
The story began on a mixed of two parallel worlds created by Mana. Both worlds are Sylvarant and Tethe'alla, are living in peace because of the Great tree of Mana, Mana created the world in order to have the energy source that is needed both for magic and to support life itself. But everything changed gravely as anyone expected, the land is dying, especially the mana. Obviously the only one that needs to solve all the problems is to have a chosen one to regenerate the world.
The story began on Sylvarant on a small town called Iselia, a group of kids named Lloyd Irving, Colette Brunel and Genis Sage, along with his sister Raine Sage, and a mercenary Kratos Aurion (Irving), and also Sheena Fujibayashi from Tethe'alla had traved around the world for the chosen's journey, Colette to regenarate the world from the Desians. But somehow the game has a complicated plot of the story, you see when Colette swears on her journey to visit the temples, but after that she began to feel like giving up her humanity to become an angel. After the temples that they visited, Colette's conditions worsens after she visited the temple for regenaration. Lloyd is worried about her, because he probably thinks that Colette was going to give up her humanity and die that way, so she will be reborn as an angel. Then on the visit on the TALLEST tower of salvation which is the TALLEST TOWER that leads to Derris-Kharan and a parallel tower of both worlds. So Colette gave up her life to Remiel, and Remiel trolls everyone that he needs Colette to revive the Goddess Martel. Lloyd and his party fought Remiel and defeated him at the end, and then Kratos also trolls, and betrays Lloyd's party for dragging Colette in the tower, but suddenly Yggdrassil appeared and nearly killed everyone. The party awoke and found out inside of some Desian's fortress, or what they called the "Renegades" because they got to the tower of salvation to rescue the chosen before she died and took the party to their lair. Many things happened throughout the journey for Lloyd and the others, so then Sheena suggests that they should travel to Tethe'alla to find a way to restore that world, and Colette's as well.
The story goes on after a few epic events, but the game make it more interesting which involved the summon spirits, Raine and Genis' theory of their own race, Zelos' flirting and sense of humor, Lloyd eagerness and determination, and Colette's kindness, and ultimately Lloyd's real father, Kratos.

Fate/Extella is a niche port of a Mousu game that has appeared on a variety of consoles. Fans of Dragon Quest Heroes or Hyrule Warriors will enjoy the similar gameplay. This particular version of the universe is set in one of the many alternate versions of the Fate universe, which is a visual novel series that has expanded to include anime, manga, light novels, and a plethora of other things. Extella is a sequal to a line of games that are set in a computer simulation. This conceit allows for popular characters from all across the property to make playable appearences.
The game plays at a nice 60fps. You can tweak game options with a launcher hidden in a menu in your steam library by right clicking over the game title. Audio is subtitled in English and offers other language options, but it is performed well. The in game audio seems to get louder during attacks, but that may just be due to the repeating attack sounds stacking on each other. The in game environments look fine and are meant to call back to specific parts of different properties. Character models are okay, but the art style tries to adapt a shiny anime look that makes some character models like Nero look really bad. The controls on an Xbox 360 controller work perfectly and are logical. I would not recommend playing this on a keyboard. You need buttons and a pad.
The game offers three campaigns and some "side missions." You have to exit a campaign to do the side missions that you unlock during gameplay. These excersions feel like padding, since you are replaying missions from the main stories and I do not understand why a menu doesn't exist in the story mode as a conveinence to allow you to access all of the content in one place, since you unlock items for your main game.The in game menus are sort of clunky with odd English translations and buried key menus, but they are servicable. The English dialogue translations feel overwrought and read like they have been written by a non-nativespeaker. Word translations and sentence structures are often clunky and I feel pulled out of the game by the experience. The effect cheapens the overall production. I can still follow the plot and I do like the characters, but my enjoyment of the game is probably due to my love for the anime property. The overall narrative has very little buy in for me up front, since the first game is a PSP/VITA exclusive that I have not played and we did not recieve the second game. The first game is due for an anime release next year in Japan, so perhaps we will see an adaptation in other countries in a few years. New fans to the Fate series will probably be completely lost. An in game glossery of terms helps fill in the gaps, but the ideas are hard to understand if you are completely new to the notions the game is trying to explain.
I am glad this was brought to this platform since I do feel that it is worth the money. How much enjoyment you will find here will depend on if you like the hack and slash genre and if you enjoy the Fate series. Consider watching one of the anime on Netflix and see if you enjoy it before jumping in.

Literally, is there a shark setting for this game? Love it. But the sharks... F***ing sharks. Literally every minute of every day, every where.. sharks. One even glitched through the sand and killed me and I wasnt even underwater, my feet were.. If you kill the shark, another one respawns moments after as the neverf***ingendingshark.
But seriously, less sharks would be nice. This game is awesome and would be 1000 times better if sharks werent everywhere every time I get in to the water. It would be far more rewarding of an experience to encounter them lurking but not as aggressive and not right off shore in 2 feet of water. Its just annoying that I know every single time I get into the water I know I will have to battle with a tigerf***ingshark within 10-15 seconds, and if you have been near the shoreline one is probably already stalking you before you even get in, takes somes realism out of the game.
With that said, its an awesome game with huge potential. An awesome change of pace from all the shooter battle royale zombie apocalypse survival looting online multiplayer game.
PROS:
- Super chill and fun with awesome moments, from starting a fire at sunset and cooking up some freshly caught fish to diving into the crysal clear water deep into shipwrecks in an ocean full of sea creatures (minus the never ending shark attacks)

- Not expensive
- Graphics feel very real at times
- Diving is awesome
CONS:
- Days seem to go too quick, maybe that creates the sense of urgency you feel while trying to survive, but it to me is too short. I would like time to take in the surroundings and not be full out running to every activity I need to do and never really getting the time to enjoy and take in the game.
- Glitches are tolerable
- Only one save point
SUGGESTIONS:
- Make the days longer
- Allow multiple save points, nothing is more aggravating than having a glitch ruin a game, it has only happened once, but it was the first game I played, by the time I traveled to the 3rd island the screen blacked out while I was sailing and the previous save point kept reproducing the same glitch, since then I have played one other game where I have been alive for several months and I got the same glitch but luckily the previous restart point corrected the issue that time

TIPS: Make sure you save often, glitches can ruin your day.. Keep you kindling next to your firepit.. I just cook food by setting it on top of the fire when traveling nomadically looting.. By far the hardest of the Chicken Invaders trilogy on Steam (CI3,4,5). As someone who gets frustrated easily, i find this title a little beyond acceptable in the sadism stakes. I'll explain why.
In most of the traditional top-down or bullet-hell shooters i've played there is a pattern to foes, there are gaps between projectiles, there are tactics to be learned, there is timing to be practiced. Chicken Invaders 3 keeps up with these traditions for the most part, but is ruined by a handful of levels which throw these features out of the window. You can be having the best run of your life, having practiced and learned the movements of foes and general projectile release ideas and filled in the rest with your own reactions and nous. Then you reach a level called "Chicken Square Dance" or "Chicken Geometry" which are completely random and invade all possible safe-spaces without any measurable consistancies or rotas. It's not projectiles that get in the way, it's the foes themselves you'll get wiped-out by.
It's REALLY annoying.
The end-zone bosses are more imaginative than in CI5, but the keyboard repetition sensor is not as good as in either of the two sequels so you can't fire as quickly in this game, also the weapons overheat a lot more easily.
Do i recommend it? Hmmmm. It's not as good as CI4; that game is this series' peak, but i do think CI3 is better than CI5 (which i gave a thumbs-down to). Yes, i would recommend it but only as an introduction to the series or for those who like their shooters to be bordering on unfair. But seriously, just get CI4 if you only want to buy one of these titles.

I have never reviewed a game before, but after reading so many reviews of others, I wanted to express my opinion.  Whether or not I can recommend the game is dependent upon what you seek, and what your expectations are.
The biggest problem, from what I have inferred from reading reviews, is from disapointed expectations.  Civilization V and earlier Firaxis/Sid Meier games are nothing short of brilliant.  The entire Civilization series (and I have been there since its inception) could arguably be labeled the greatest PC games ever produced, from every which way you might want to analyze it: quality, depth, re-playablility, customization, fun, and strategy.
If you are looking for Starships to have the depth, and strategy (long-term planning and maneuvering) to achieve the final victory, you won't find that here.  This is a simple game, almost more like an arcade game with some choice elements to be determined by your preference, such as do you want firepower or stealth?  But not the intricies of long-term grand scale strategy that Civ is famous for.  If you are anticipating even a scaled-down version of Civ, you will be disappoineted.  This is not a game of watching your grand design come to frutuion.   After having played several games of Civilization V, marathons that lasted more than 800 turns and a week of playing per game, I welcome being able to play a quick in-and-out game like this.  This is more complicated than Solitaire or Minesweeper, and can be similarly addicitve.  Starships is NOT trying to be Civ.  Perhaps Firaxis went too far away from strategy on this one, but I had fun with it.    Simple fun.
However, I was really disappointed the way ship design and outfitting work.  When I first heard about this release , I thought back to one of my all-time favortie games, Master of Orion II, and shrilled at the prospect of a Sid Meier version of this.  In MOO2, you selected a ship class, which was an empty shell, and you chose how to outfit it, based upon the research you had done.  And even if you were capable of adding your Class X shields to your ship, you could have instead installed Class V shields, allowing more space for other modules (such as another array of lasers) and reducing its cost.   And there were several choices of laser technology to add, based on research and function.   In Starships, there are only lasers (long-range) and plasma cannons (short range), with only a nebulous upgrade by incrementing a level.  I was looking forward to specialized intricate ship design.  There is none of that, as this is the simplest system.  For me, the ship designing  in MOO2 was the most exciting part of any Space 4X game I have ever played, and what I was hoping  Starships would be.  Based upon my expectation, my desire, this game fails.
Does this game have depth?  No.  Is the strategy a deep-thinking man's game like Civ?  No.  Was it fun?   Yes.    What you want from a game, the level of complexity and granularity you enjoy,  together with your expectation of Starships, will determine whether you think it is worth it ot not.    For some easy, casual and quick fun, Starships delivers.  But if you want this to be a CIv-like game, or somewhat like MOO2, complicated and full of strategic and tactical choices, it will not satisfy.

For the price I did not expect a game that would blow me away. I expected a polished simple single player experience and that is exactly what I got.
At first I was slightly disappointed in the introduction video. It should at the very least scale up to 1080p, but it is a minor aestethic complaint. Next I was confounded by the "Settings". Basically you can only choose between windowed or fullscreen, and you can adjust various volume levels. Thats it. Further on it becomes obvious that you will not need any advanced settings for this game.
Visually the game delivers a polished, clean and smooth experience. Various icons and symbols ties nicely in with Beyond Earth. Aduio effects are also very BEish.
Strategically you manage planets and one fleet of spaceships through resources produced by said planets and rewards from missions. You have to choose missions wisely because you can only complete so many each turn and those you ignore will be completed by your neighbours.
Tactically you move around and attack enemies on various "maps" generated for each battle and there are a handful of random elements thrown in for each battle.  You configure your ships offense based on preferred range and utility, and you have a few defensive options as well.
The whole thing ties together nicely and offer a relaxed, balanced single player experience. I can easily recommend this game.
