This is how this game works. You buy the game, watch the tutorial, get excited, build your first ship, first ship sinks, you go back to the drawing board, you make improvements, Ship works YAY, you get excited, you spawn a small enemy ship, you blow it to bits, you feel accomplished you spawn 2 small enemy ships you blow them to bits, you start to have faith in your design, so you spawn a bigger enemy, and guess what happens there, YOU get blown to bits, you cry, rage quit the game and go to sleep, after all you've been playing for 7 hours straight. During your sleep, you get a dream about a new stronger design, you either wake in the middle of the night with excitement or wait untill morning, anyways, you construct your new improved and mighty ship, you spawn the bigger ship that blew you to bits hopeing for revenge, 20 seconds later you're inches away from breaking your monitor as your ammo caches gets hit by a stray shell from his cannon and makes a majestic explosion. You ralise, armour is the solution, so you go back to the drawing board and make the most armoured ship you can, you release it in the water....it sinks, you keep trying and it keeps sinking....you're frustratd, insecure, you have lost faith in your designs, you think you cant play this game anymore, but it's too late you already played 20 hours of it in the first 2 days, you realise you cannot give up. You then open ol' trusty google and youtube you scour them for as much information as you can. 7 hours of research later and a few physics lessons from your old school book read on the way. You become a ship building expert, you then use your new found knowledge to design the ultimate boat to crush your fearsome enemy and then...... SUCCESS!! You have sunk the enemy ship. You feel good about yourself, go fap and go to sleep all happy feeling like a worthy engineer. You wake up next morning thinking "Hey, I wanna try my luck with the campaign" You start the campaign, remember you still have some left over confidence from that battle in the designer mode, first thing that happens in the campaign, you get attacked by a dingy you feel even more confident and actually for a second believe you can win this campaign. 20 mins later, you get attacked by the Deep Water Guard Crazy Chicken Armada. You look at that vessel in disbelief, cursing the day you bought this game (which is about 3 days ago) and the Crazy Chicken blows you and you fleet to smithereens....you rage quit and you rinse and repeat the above.
11/10 would buy again.

I was in the office, bored as a clam... browsing the Steam Store for something new that I could play once I got home, I saw this, and since I really like Minecraft, Legos, any game that gives me the chance to build and design I purchased this bad boy, and boy did I got a bargain.
Started the game and took a head on dive into Creative mode.
At first the quantity of things appearing on screen can be a bit overwhelming, the game tries to solve this with a few tutorials and hints on screen. At the beginning it will ask about the building mode you will want to use. If you're like me you're gonna end up using both, according to what you do.
There is a briefly steep leaning curve, but thanks to modern technology you can always resort to the all mighty Google and his loyal servant Youtube. So saying the game is complex and hard is really no excuse at all, maybe you're just a bit lazy.
Your first constructs will be floating blocks of wood that will be more dangerous to themselves than to their enemy, you will do boats that do backflips and roll over. You will build and destroy your creations over and over again. And then, maybe finally you start getting the hang of it, and you will be astounded with the great differences between your first builds and the last ones.
You will come up with a crazy idea in the middle of the night and you will stop whatever the hell you're doing because you MUST see if you can come up with this huge deadly AP quad cannon.
The creative mode is all fun and games, because you don't have any impediments about realizing your most wildly ideas about naval warfare and what not because everything its free.
The fun part of this game, it's the campaign, this game mode is a trial by fire. If you don't know how to properly manage your resources and device constructs that can repel and counter the attacks you will suffer, you're gonna get your robotic♥♥♥♥♥kicked and then some more. Thankfully, thanks to the incredible huge versatility we have during building, the possibilities to overcome any and all challenges are endless.
Huge♥♥♥♥♥cannons are a little bit OP and you can totally pummel anything that's within your range. There's tons of options about proper defense, anti missiles missiles, anti missiles laser systems (this last one can be quite the ♥♥♥♥♥ to proper build, I suggest using youtube) and thanks to the last update we have LUA programming for even more dangerous weapons of mass destruction. The naval AI can be a little clunky sometimes, but it's ok.
It you like designing and tweek around, this is the game for you, it may be a little complicated at first, but once you get the hang of it, you start gliding on the build mode doing awesome things in really no time.
I for one really liked this game, the community is great, the devs are great, this is a solid 10/10. I can hardly believe its still on Alpha, once we get the full release I most likely will die from a stroke because of the excitement. But hey, it was worth it.

Dark Souls is a game of two extremes. In limbo, if you will.
On one hand its a game filled with death, misery and dispair. Its carefully crafted world of Lordran is a rotting kingdom where everything is out to get you. Everything, from its many inhabitants, to its environments to the random encounters with other players are solely there to ruin your day. Its environments are macabre and often grotesque, which is match by some of its enemies. And, of course, the game is hard. Brutally hard at times. All of your achievements can be wiped away in a second. The game can and will pin you to the ground and leave you there if you let it.
But, on the other hand, it is a game filled with life, joy and hope. The many messages left by other players are there to cheer you on, to lean you onto a secret or just to make you laugh. The bloodstains are there to show you that other players are having just as bad a time as you are. Its environments are starkly beautiful, and show that there is still a shimmer of light in Lordran. And, finally, it is fair game. No matter how many times you die, the game encourages you to push on and to
give up. The game encourages you to change or upgrade your equipment and encourages you to change your playstyle. Other players are there to help you during boss fights. Ultimately, the game
you to become a better player and it
you to succeed.
The message of Dark Souls is that death will come to us all. Everyone. You, your family, your friends, the world around will die eventually. But even through the hardships and hopelessness of life, there is always a light at the end of the tunnel. How you make the best of life is up to you. The best you can do out of life is to keep going. All until the light fades.
Thank you for reading this.

This is potentially a great game. The mechanics are wonderful. It runs very fast and smooth and i do love a good meta-strategic long-game.
HOWEVER. beginning the game even with assistance of an experienced player is a long, frustrating and unrewarding experience.
First you're going to have to get to grips with a very fast, hotkey based control system. -which is great - except you can't modify the keys to your liking so if you're intuitive and fast with another game or program you're going to have to UNLEARN all of that first.
Right now i can't stop hitting E because i use it to pitch in a couple of other games (those games allow me to tune the controls when a button clashes) but FTD forces me into a tactical map view about once a minute.
FOR THE LOVE OF BISCUITS WHY CANT I REMAP CONTROLS?
Also you are in two places. you have an avatar for some reason. No idea why since it's invincible, doesnt do the construction and has such bizarre movement characteristics that you never want to be first person viewing.
The second viewpoint is a sort of spectator-cam that moves at supersonic speed with a momentary blip on the directional key. -again adding to the feeling of being trapped in a clumsy, jerky body with no influence on surroundings.
OK, putting all this aside you set about trying to learn the ropes 'cause it looks like fun once you know them.
You have a few options:
Vehicle Designer - infinite resources, virtually nothing to restrain you or drive your build. What am i building for? oh, the campaign. but i have no idea what works in campain. 'cause i'm here trying to get ready for campaign. SO i place blocks for an hour or two, get bored with how awful they look and exit to main menu.
Campaign - i go to start campaign since many games use missions as a way to introduce game concepts - Offering microgoals to help the player understand mechanics and priorities - maybe this game will be like that. Nope. Just plopped on a raft in the middle of a hostile ocean with 5 factions at high development levels and minimal pointers on how to even begin to gather resources.
Multiplayer - obviously a place you go once the new player skill-cliff is a distant nightmare. I can't offer you any reports on this.
I'm glad i own this game because when it's done it could be wonderful but having to re-train my hands to use it simply because the devs won't let players remap controls spoils the experience enormously.
TLDR: Great potential. Maybe awesome if you've been playing since day one and all the complexity got added underneath you but it's becoming inaccessible to new players. Too little reward for your time.

LUFTRAUSERS is a great, fun minigame. If you are looking for a quick, enjoyable, session; then this game is for you.

LUFTRAUSERS is pretty much what it looks like: an arcade dogfighter. I was expecting a story mode or something similar, but all I got was a straightforward 2D shoot-em-up. That having been said, I am not in the least disappointed by what I received; this game knows what it does and does it well. It provides the classic arcade experience of scoring as much as possible without dying, throwing in for bonus the rush of excitement when you stall in midair, watching hordes of enemies and waves of bullets streak past you in a whirlwind of death. The stalling mechanic is really what makes this game so good; you can stop accelerating and simply let gravity do the work of dodging hazards for you, then after changing direction speed up at the last second and escape the jaws of death. Obviously it's not a lot of content, despite the number of ship parts allowing for a commendable combination of ships and thus playstyles. For what I paid, however, I'd say I easily got my money's worth.

This game is absoulutely awesome!
intro.
i'm not sure i've ever seen any intro in most of tower defence games that i've ever played. but i'm reckoned that usually if a game has some intro, usually its a better game than without - or - in other words - game should worth making intro for it )
warstone greets you with neatly done intro that immediately shows you a gameplay and opens a story - great user experience where small, short, quick piece of recorded gameplay just teases you what is going to be next.
tutorial.
tutorial is usually another thing bad games don't have and good games have. I've met couple of games i just didn't realize how to play until i found some video on tube ))) here you have a magician and some kind of "God's hand" that arrives from a sky and give you the basics when you are towerdefense newbie or useful hints.
this kind of tutorial is another greatly developed, сarefully thought out solution when you don't have to play separate boring "tutorial" game chapter, but instead just play the game, seamlessly and transparently immersing into its world.
tower defense.
in fact, in this game you don't have towers (or maybe i just didn't play it long enought yet) - instead of towers you have heroes - and i think it changes the game perception a lot. especially adding a possiblity to make a great level where you both attact and defend: one units stop walking enemies, other units walk the route while enemy plays tower defence trying to stop your forces! i've never seen anything similar in any tower defense game before - and yes, these are units instead of towers that made this real - because walking towers would be nonsense :)))
base.
usually most towerdefence games has one single ui where only levels are changing, and some popups appear - this one has a whole big city base where  you build different buildings that open new units, you have magician to tell you a big and interesting story with lots of details, the market where you can buy the spells, arena, where you make multiplayer games - that - attention - are part of mission!
gameplay.
after all these things i wrote about you might be already reckoned that its a game of good quality, but you didn't yet try the gameplay - and its absolutely fabulous - games not quite hard to make you to refuse trying over and over, buts its quite competitive when you feel  you can win if you try little better, and, then, you can get a star if you try little harder once more. stars are not given just for perfect lavels, but for achieving a special condition in a perfect level, which, again, makes each level and a process of getting each star more interesting.
most tower defence games are predictable - when you can just get the biggest gun and stop all enemies waves; warstone is greatly balanced and that keeps you immersed: the very moment  you thing everything is under control you get some new kind of monsters that are invulnerable to your current troops and  you need to make new desicions, use magic, use lightning, magician comes out with fresh hint,  you are always limited with resources - so you cannot waste them...
early access.
i was expecting something is still being developed - but i got the game that works and performs perfectly. perhaps the only thing about "early access" is that levels are added while i play! once i entered the game a collaborative level was promiced, the next day it was already present!
conclusion.
this is a game that should be voted for and should be getting the big international prizes, media attention, and love of gamers, as it perfectly does what a game is invented for - it entertains, it makes you rest, it makes you PLAY.

A game that does justice to it's source material AND provides fun and engaging content. This is a must-buy if you like top shelf action games (like Uncharted, Tomb Raider, Far Cry) and/or are a fan of the Lord of the Rings movies/books. Either one will do!
I'm going to start with this because it was my favourite part - this game expands on the content seen in the movies in the best possible way. You get to learn more about the creation of the Rings of Power (through cut scenes and dialogue), daily life in Middle-Earth (through content found by exploring), and get to see
without his iconic armour. Almost every main character is well developed, and the Orc warchiefs you encounter (... mini bosses) all have character.
The graphics are great, even by (the end of...) 2017's standards. The combat is SO fun - it requires some skill and it never felt like a slog/boring - and it makes the most out of limited enemy types and simple controls. The Nemesis system is neat, allowing you to brain-wash mini-bosses to do your bidding... and the character development system allows you to increase your abilities to a satisfying degree without feeling super-overpowered by the end of an average playthrough (you can't just button mash your way through the whole game).
If you enjoyed the LOTR/Hobbit movies or books AND you enjoy a good action game every once in awhile, this does both REALLY well and comes in a cheaply priced, tidy package.

I've been a fan of the Ace Combat series since AC4 came out for the PS2. I remember being reluctant to try it at first because I've been a lifelong fan of flight sims but after accepting the fact that they threw realism out the window, I was able to enjoy AC4 for what it was--fun, pure and simple. AC5 and Zero added memorable (if not ridiculous) stories, while improving the system for purchasing or upgrading planes. I really got attached to some of the planes and it almost seemed sad to buy a better plane. And did I mention that the games were FUN? AC6 was a bit of a letdown; story was less memorable and it seemed like you had to take a new plane every mission, but it was still FUN! So with that in mind, I purchased Assault Horizon, aware that it had shortcomings but figuring that I could at least have fun. Boy was I wrong...I've played 5 missions so far and I have little motivation to continue. One word sums up the gameplay: BORING. The AC-130 mission got old after a few minutes. The helicopter mission was three times as long as it needed to be and was pretty much just doing the same thing over and over. And the aircraft missions...the one thing that should still have been exciting, regardless of everything else...how the heck did they manage to screw these up? Dull, boring, and much of it felt like a task instead of a game. I can't believe I'm saying this acout an Ace Combat game.

I can't do it. I tried it on PS4 and on PC and I can't enjoy this game. To be fair, this port is excellent*, but I can't defend the game.
There is a lot of VN stuff here, and if you want Tamamo or Nero as your doting waifu, this game lays that on SO INCREDIBLY THICK in the VN segments that your teeth will rot from the sweetness.
The musou part of the game? It's... perfectly playable. I really have nothing bad to say about it for the sorts of people who just muck with musous for fun, to enjoy themselves. There's a lot of flash, a lot of style, and a lot of waifus on offer (Though you won't get a free pick of them until you knock out large chunks of the games' main story arcs.)
But I just can't stand the musou parts of the game. There is nothing to your movesets. The levels are just great big colorful cyberboxes where you warp from zone to zone. At each zone, you have to stop and kill about 500 mooks to spawn the midbosses, kill two of them, kill another 500 (Triggering the "Holy cow chief, you killed 1000? You are a true warrior of the holy grail!" message all of 40 seconds into the fight.), kill the second set of midbosses, then you finally have the zone and now have to do that eight or nine more times throughout the map. This same kill, boss, kill, boss pattern is also how you do defense, so it takes just as long to repel an attack and shut your teammates whining for help up than it does to secure a new zone.
If killing things were interesting in Extella, that would be fine. But it isn't. You do not have a Basara moveset. You barely have a Warriors moveset. While the moves are big, flashy, hit wide areas, and generally have an anime sensibility to them, they just aren't interesting. And the stop-and-go pace just drags each mission out tremendously. There is no fancy strategy or gimmick or story to be told in these levels, just the story of someone who has to walk to each room and slowly, laboriously clear it out while listening to your allies moan and wish you stopped attacking to clear out THEIR room. Any time the game gets clever mid-mission, it usually involves you clearing EVEN MORE rooms and making your conquest of the map nearly sisyphean. Worse, your musou attack is probably the least satisfying and most pointlessly long special move I've ever seen. Your ultras are cool, but they are kinda big skippable corny anime cutscenes appropriate to the Fate franchise. But you don't get those but once a match maybe and you'll probably mash that musou button most of the fight. The entire thing feels like an amateur's first musou, and that's really what it is. I rag on Senran Kagura, but Senran brings a lot better stuff to the table... like Yumi, for instance.
These are all little things, but they add up. They may not be a big deal to you, really. But if you're the sort who noticed that Samurai Warriors 4-2 just completely bungled large parts of the combat, or that One Piece Pirate Warriors 3 was secretly the best musou Koei had done, if you know what Sengoku Basara even is or why someone would want to play it, if you're a musou connosieur, I don't think Fate Extella will fit the bill for you.
That's not to say Extella is a bad game. I mean, I can't stand it and I think it's barely playable trash, but what is there, what effort they've put in, and the sheer amount of Fate fan-service... There's an audience for this game. If you aren't a musou snob, and you like the idea of having Tamamo and Nero practically beat the stuffing out of each other to prove which one loves you more, this might end up being something you like. But I can't enjoy it.
*EDIT: By excellent, I mean it runs smooth and loads quick. I don't think it is hitting 60 FPS though, though the action isn't all that interesting enough to merit it, but I can understand disagreements on the issue.

Vlambeer: a studio known for its outstanding design skills and dedication to retro-inspired games that deliver fast action without getting hung up on anything that isn’t directly related to the core gameplay. This studio has proven itself time and time again with its catalogue of fast-action games. It should therefore come as no surprise to one acquainted with the two-man team’s previous releases that LUFTRAUSERS is a game of the same variety. It should also come as no surprise to hear that; like those games; it is also an undoubtedly outstanding piece of work.
The core gameplay of LUFTRAUSERS is centred on the destruction of enemy aircraft, naval vessels and blimps (the latter of which only appear once you’re scoring big). Like other shmups LUFTRAUSERS likes to throw wave after wave of enemies at you. In this case there’s a little more room to manoeuvre than what one might be used to in a bog-standard shmup. It’s possible to scroll the screen left or right and continue flying in either direction indefinitely as you contend with the limitless supply of opponents for your blood. Destroying enemies earns the player points and as one’s score increases so too does the severity of the threat posed by the enemy. Each time an enemy is killed, the player’s score multiplier goes up by one. Keeping that multiplier high is the key to getting the best scores. It’s a very simple concept, but it lends itself to create some interesting gameplay scenarios. Do you go chase down that swarm of fighters in order to raise your multiplier before sinking the nearby battleship? Or do you attack the ship first and take the fighters on afterwards? The former has the potential to yield a greater final score, but it’s worth bearing in mind that dodging AA fire is no joke. The latter is the safer option, but you’re not going to get as many points that way. Players just starting out are likely to only witness some fighters and gun boats, but those racking up big scores will quickly find themselves facing off against large numbers of battleships, aircraft equipped with laser weapons and eventually the dreaded blimps. Stronger enemies yield more points, so the more of them you kill the better your score becomes, but that comes at the expense of inviting further trouble in the form of more of those strong enemies showing up to blow you out of the sky (which
happen sooner or later, as is the case with games featuring what one might call ‘survival-mode’ style gameplay).
A Rauser is comprised of three components: a weapon, body and engine. Specific components from each category can be swapped in and out upon returning to the menus, allowing you to find a perfect match that suits your playstyle. Some of the available choices are fairly conventional, while others are somewhat less so. Want to fly a jet with a conventional machine gun built into the nose? Fine. What about a plane that propels itself through the sky by firing bullets from its tail-end, while incinerating those in front of it with a high-powered laser? It’s done. Or maybe an aircraft that can dive under the waves and surface under enemy ships, sinking them with a single-shot cannon that releases additional projectiles in all directions after the initial projectile’s impact? Not a problem. Every part has a number of small-scale tasks associated with it, such as defeating a certain number of enemies whilst maintaining a combo, or killing enough enemies of a specific type. Successfully completing these tasks usually unlocks either new parts or new colour schemes. Most of these short-term goals are fun to pursue and encourage a bit of experimentation. Even if you have a favourite combination of parts, it’s fun to go after some of these while trying out parts which you might not normally go for.
The world of LUFTRAUSERS is depicted through pixel art, something that a good number of indie games have chosen to go for. The visual style goes a long way in contributing towards the ‘arcade-like’ feel that the game has - a retro-inspired art style for a retro-inspired game. The default colour scheme keeps things simple enough so that it’s always easy to keep track of what’s going on, while the effective use of silhouettes in place of highly detailed sprites allows your imagination to fill in the blanks. Some of the alternate colour schemes are less appealing, thanks to some colour combinations that just don’t match-up, either because the contrast between colours is too great or because the scheme feels dull in comparison to the default one.
KOZILEK’s main theme fits the game well enough, but what really stands out here is how the instruments used to play the said theme change depending on which parts you’ve got equipped. It’s a nice little touch that keeps things fresh. The sound effects themselves also do a great job of helping to maintain that retro feel, and sound like they came straight out of an 8-bit game.
LUFTRAUSERS is another example of a game made by a studio that knows its target audience inside-out. It’s a stellar example of an arcade-style game done right – it knows it’s a straightforward, pick-up-and-play game, so it focuses purely on what matters most for that type of game: the core gameplay experience. Put simply if you’re a fan of the ‘instant-action’ games that Vlambeer has put out in the past then chances are LUFTRAUSERS is one game you can’t afford to miss out on.

LUFTRAUSERS is a bullet hell airplane based game, being released on PC, PS3 and Vita in early 2014.
Game play is quite simple, you are in control of a airplane and you have to take on hundreds and hundreds of other enemy fighters coming at you from all angles. This game allows your plane to fly in all 360 degrees. Your main weapon will shoot from the front of your plane, you also have to take into consideration things like gravity, stalling and drifting whilst dodging all of the oncoming enemies.  Initially the controls seem very hard to get a grasp of, but once you work out how the plane flies and how you are supposed to control it, it becomes almost second nature. I would say it took me at least an hour to get to grips with the controls.
Graphically, the game has a very minimalist look to it. Whilst there is little detail gone into the planes and their silhouettes, you still feel like you are actually there in the skies shooting the planes down yourself.  They could of quite easily made this look like a many of the other flight games on Steam, I think its the graphics and art style that most people will remember this game for.
There isn't really any story or plot to follow in LUFTRAUSERS. I also didn't really want one too; it's perfectly fine for a game not to have a plot I think. After all, your character can nose dive your plane into an enemy battleship, reap the rewards from it and move onto the next character without batting an eyelid.
The game also has a kind of rogue-like feel to it, after each level, you are able to customize your plane with different weapons and armor, and you keep all of the updates even after you die, along with any levels and points you have earned. Eventually you'll get more powerful and be able to simply overpower some stages purely because your plane will be kitted up so much.
LUFTRAUSERS is a very hard game. I have died countless times, you just need to get used to it - there is no way around it. But if you preserver through, you'll soon be able to break through that wall you have been pounding your head on for an hour and beat the challenges that are set at the start of each level.  In order for me to reach the "end", it took me just over five hours. For me it felt just about right as I think it would really start to get tedious if I had to keep playing.
This is probably a game you will want to dip into now and then, and not do a full stint of it like me, to get maximum fun out of it, just play it for twenty minutes at a time. The game is also highly recommended you use a game pad too; I tried with keyboard and it was just horrendous to control.
To sum up, LUFTRAUSERS is a nicely put together indie title with some interesting elements; bullet-hell fans will absolutely adore it, and this is really a good game to play if you have five or ten minutes to spare as no level will ever last longer than that. The price tag of £6,99 makes it an absolute bargain for anyone.
